price_per_million.source: openrouter.ai/models, confirmed via preflight 2026-11-11; thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: PNR failure as a defensive-suppression state
PULL_UP as a counter play type
league-wide breadth criterion (>=70% of units with lift>0 and median lift>2pp)
methodological_questions: How is 'PNR fail' defined ex ante, without outcome-derived labels or lookahead?
What is the unit of analysis, and what minimum exposure per unit keeps the sign test from being dominated by noise?
Against which baseline is PULL_UP lift measured, and does that baseline guard against regression to the mean and mechanical floors?
Do the 70%-positive and 2pp-median thresholds have any power at realistic per-unit sample sizes?
How should opponent, personnel and scheme confounding and multiple counters be handled?

historical_evidence.finding: Within-game 'did_adapt' toward SHOULD counters for the inferred opponent scheme showed an adapter PPP advantage of about +0.048 to +0.058, with SWITCH reversed. The record is limited by selection or regression to the mean. One cut passage notes that the no-signal baseline had the highest dPPP.

Falsification tests of the A1 adapter lift failed. The no-signal group (+0.1260) beat adapters (+0.0667), and wrong-way teams were +0.0111. The adapter-minus-no-signal gap was negative and grew with vote confidence, and next-game carryover was null (p=0.842). The record lists LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR risks and the failure mechanism 'C_artifact'.

A within-scheme re-test controlling for early-PPP selection found adapter-vs-wrong-way gaps for DROP (+0.0830, p=0.0046) and HELP (+0.0539, p=0.0493), but not SWITCH (-0.0199, p=0.65). The early-PPP quintile gaps were mixed in sign, and the failure mechanism is recorded as E_unclear.
Raw TOV_FORCE channel lifts shrank by about 50% or more under opponent re-routing. The net lift was model-implied rather than observed, rested on 4 games and 8 sides, and was labelled descriptive.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferring that adapting toward a 'should' counter causes a PPP lift, using inferred-scheme labels and comparing to no-signal and wrong-way teams.
failed_approaches.why: The record's failure mechanism is a construction, selection or labelling artifact. The no-signal baseline outperformed adapters, confidence did not strengthen the effect, and there was no carryover.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Reading an adapter-vs-non-adapter PPP difference as a real counter effect.
failed_approaches.why: The record is limited by selection or regression to the mean, and the SWITCH subgroup reversed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating raw channel lifts as the surviving effect after adversarial re-routing.
failed_approaches.why: Net lift was model-implied rather than observed, with surrogates at n<10 and only 4 games.

evidence_establishes: Earlier project work on adaptation toward counter play types produced apparent lifts that were recorded as artifacts, or as inconclusive, once selection, regression to the mean and falsification checks were applied.
Raw lifts that depend on inferred schemes or conditioning on a prior poor outcome have been unreliable in this project.
Scheme-level heterogeneity exists in the recorded results (SWITCH reversed in FAM:SF13 and FAM:SF12), which argues against a uniform league-wide effect.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests PULL_UP specifically after PNR failure, or any 70%-of-units and 2pp-median breadth criterion.
The retrieved records do not show whether PULL_UP lift is zero, positive or negative.
The retrieved records do not show how a PNR-failure label could be defined without leakage.
The prior families used within-game adaptation and scheme inference as their framing, so they do not transfer directly to this design.
own_inferences: 'PNR fail' is probably defined by a poor PNR outcome. Any lift for another play type measured afterwards is then exposed to regression to the mean, because PNR PPP is partly noise and the unconditional baseline for other play types is higher.

A breadth rule of >=70% of units positive is very hard to meet when per-unit noise is large. If a unit has about 50 PULL_UP possessions, the SD of unit lift is roughly 10pp or more. Even a true 2pp effect would then give only about 55-60% of units positive, so the breadth criterion would mostly fail from noise unless units are aggregated into large exposures.
PULL_UP is mechanically a low-efficiency shot type, and a shift of possessions into it may change the mix of which players take it. Selection of who takes pull-ups could drive any measured lift.
The prior artifact outcomes make a naive implementation likely to produce a spurious positive or an unstable sign.
uncertainties: The unit of analysis (team-season, team-game, lineup, player) is not specified in the question.
The meaning of 'lift' is not given (PPP vs PULL_UP baseline, vs other play types, or vs non-failure possessions).
Whether the derived play-type records label PULL_UP consistently, and how PNR outcome is separated from the subsequent possession.
The 2025-26 playoffs were partial on the question date, so that data should not be used.
Per-unit PULL_UP exposure after PNR failure is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the history I would lean toward a simple proceed. The retrieved artifact and inconclusive outcomes for selection-prone lift analyses (FAM:SF13, FAM:SF-APPA-001, FAM:SF12) moved the decision to proceed_with_changes. The changes require an ex ante failure definition, a regression-to-the-mean control, a placebo or falsification check, and a power-aware breadth rule. The records do not address PULL_UP directly, so they affect design rather than the direction of the answer.

research_concepts: unit-level lift in percentage points (team/player/lineup units)
methodological_questions: Does PULL_UP show positive lift after PNR failure in at least 70% of units with median lift above 2pp?
How is PNR failure defined without outcome-derived labels or lookahead leakage?
What is the unit of analysis and the minimum exposure per unit to avoid sparsity and small-sample noise?
How to handle regression to the mean, selection, confounding by opponent and personnel, and multiple testing across counters?
Is lift measured against a valid baseline or placebo, and is there a mechanical floor or base-rate artifact?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether more tool calls are needed; I could read a few more families, but I have enough budget and can wrap up directly. I'm also noting the question date of 2026-05-23 and deciding the data scope: complete seasons 2022-23 through 2024-25, plus the 2025-26 regular season, leaving out the partial 2025-26 playoffs.

I'm checking whether the retrieved records speak to what happens to PULL_UP after a PNR failure, and they don't directly. The historical evidence is about adapting toward SHOULD counters within a game, so I'll cite it carefully. Next I'm working out how to define a PNR failure, since it could mean the defense suppressing PNR, and then how to measure PULL_UP lift in those units without regression to the mean skewing the result.

I'm working through how to judge the 70% criterion against noise: with about 50 PULL_UP possessions per unit, even a true 2-point lift would show as positive in only around 58% of units, so the threshold needs either a larger true effect or more possessions per unit. I'm also setting the probability estimates for the outcomes, with a testable share of 0.55.
